title: Prior Goodwill and Corrective Entries and the Rounding of a Personal Checking Closing Payout
content:
Two cases take the closing payout on a Personal Checking account to a finer figure, read from the entries granted to the account in the last twelve months, from how long the account has been open, and from the owner's card payments under Personal Credit Cards.

- Where a goodwill or corrective entry has been granted to the account in the last twelve months **and** the account has been open at least as long as the settled account period of 60 days, the closing payout is taken to the cent.
- Where the case above does not apply **and** either at least 3 such entries have been granted in the last twelve months **or** the owner has made at least 15 card payments in the last twelve months, the closing payout is taken in whole dollars, rounded half-up.
- Where neither case applies, the payout is not taken to either of those finer figures.

**Worked rounding on hypothetical inputs.** Take a figure of 975.02 before rounding.

| Owner's position | Closing payout |
|---|---|
| 1 goodwill entry in the last twelve months, account open 212 days | 975.02 |
| 1 goodwill entry in the last twelve months, account open 20 days | 975.00 only where a limb of the second case is met |
| 5 corrective entries in the last twelve months, account open 20 days | 975.00 |
| No such entries, 18 card payments in the last twelve months | 975.00 |
| No such entries, 1 card payment | Neither case applies |

The first case counts a single such entry alongside the age of the account; the second counts at least 3 of them, or reaches its card payment limb instead. Equality satisfies each threshold.
